newsitem.title: USA: New jobless claims rose last week.
newsitem.headline: New jobless claims rose last week.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up to claim new unemployment benefits rose last week, the government said Thursday.

The Labour Department said jobless claims climbed by 11,000 to 316,000 in the week ended Feb. 22, compared with a revised 305,000 in the previous week. Economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 310,000 for the week.
But another key yardstick -- the four-week moving average, which smooths out the more volatile weekly figures -- fell last week to its lowest level in more than six months.
The four-week average, which many economists consider to be a more reliable gauge of unemployment trends, fell to 313,250, its lowest level since the week ended Aug. 10, when it stood at 312,750.
The department said 13 states and Puerto Rico reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Feb. 15, the latest period for which that data were available.
Among the largest were California with 21,946 fewer filings, North Carolina with 3,803, Illinois with 2,661, and New York with 2,022.
California said the drop in claims was due to a work week shortened by the Lincoln's Birthday holiday, as well as fewer layoffs in the construction and food industries, and in agriculture.
North Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the textile, furniture and rubber industries, while Illinois said it had fewer layoffs in the trade industry and in manufacturing.
New York gave no reason for its decline.
No states reported an increase in initial claims exceeding 1,000 in the Feb. 15 week.
